units.text: INT. FUNICULAR CAR, MID-SLOPE - NIGHT
A wooden cabin the size of a tram, suspended on a steel cable over a pine-black ravine.
At the summit, the lights of an alpine observatory glow like a lit match.
At the bottom, a sleeping village.
In the middle, the car has stopped.
NADIA VOSKUIJLEN, 30s, sits upright on the slatted bench in a stolen maintenance coverall two sizes too large.
Dark hair scraped into a bun.
Eyes that do not blink often.
A hard case rests between her boots.
Across from her, "SPOON" TEMBO, 50s, round-faced, soft-spoken, a retired watchmaker with a splitting grin and a spoon-handle toothpick he rolls between his teeth.
He wears the same coverall, neatly pressed.
The car sways.
The cable creaks.
Outside, a lonely crow lifts off the rail.
Nadia. It stopped.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: I felt it.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: It is not supposed to stop.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: Nothing is supposed to stop, Spoon. Everything does.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: He leans to the window.
Far above, a floodlight sweeps along the cable and draws near, a white bar crossing the snow.
Get down.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Spoon drops to the floor.
She slides off the bench beside him and pulls the case in against her ribs.
The light washes the cabin white, holds for three terrible seconds, and moves on.
Neither breathes.
The cable creaks again.
Then a hollow clank somewhere above, and the car lurches one foot downhill and stops.
They have cut the power.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: They haven't. They don't know we're here.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Then why did it stop?
units.name: SPOON

units.text: Because Eddie was supposed to hold the relay and Eddie is a coward.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Eddie is a nice young man.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: Eddie is a nice young man who has probably gone home.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: A relay clunks in the machinery overhead, and a distant motor begins to cycle, a slow metal countdown.
Nadia's lips part.
She mouths a number at Spoon: two minutes.
Spoon nods slowly, his toothpick stilled.
They crouch in the dark, listening to the wind comb the pines.
Nadia. What if the vault is empty?
units.name: SPOON

units.text: Then we've climbed a mountain for nothing.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: I like nothing. I have a great deal of it at home.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: She almost laughs.
She presses the back of her hand to her mouth.
The brake releases with a long sigh.
The cable tightens.
The car begins to glide uphill again, smooth as milk, and the tension in the cabin goes out of both of them like air from a bellows.
Spoon sits back up on the bench.
Nadia slumps against the wall.
My heart, I think it left in the last minute.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: Mine's in the case.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: She taps the lid.
He chuckles, a warm sound in a cold box.
The observatory grows larger in the window.
Its dome opens like an eye.
When we step out, you're not Spoon anymore.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: No?
units.name: SPOON

units.text: You're Doctor Aurelio Stahl, from the Geneva office.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Doctor Stahl, at your service.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: Lower.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Doctor Stahl, at your very humble service.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: She shakes her head.
The car glides into the station.
Doors hiss open on yellow light and the smell of machine oil.
Shoulders back, Doctor.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Spoons are always bent, my dear. But I will try.
units.name: SPOON

units.text: They step out together into the light.
